value: There was a negative relationship between symptoms and the supplementary motor area, precentral gyrus, cuneus, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex during Reappraise > Look-Negative.

Post-hoc analyses showed that anxiety symptoms predicted decreased precentral gyrus, cuneus, and dACC activation, whereas depression symptoms were not related to these regions; depression symptoms predicted decreased SMA activation, while anxiety symptoms were not related.

These findings suggest that anxiety and depression are negatively associated with deficiencies recruiting a broader neural network during cognitive reappraisal, with under-engagement of the dACC and additional cortical regions more closely tied to anxiety symptoms.
